/arbor # BharatContract AI — 8-Hour Autonomous Engineering & Research Integrity Mission ## Mission You are operating in the existing BharatContract AI repository using the Arbor skill and the Beam 1.0 model. Your task is to make the project measurably more correct, reliable, testable, and defensible as a college research project. Work autonomously for up to 8 hours, with an absolute maximum of 10 hours, subject to the runtime and tool limits of the environment. Do not spend time merely generating documentation, repeatedly inspecting the same files, or making cosmetic changes. Prioritize demonstrable correctness improvements, independent tests, failure analysis, and reproducible evidence. **The objective is verified engineering progress, not maximum lines of code or maximum number of completed tasks.** ## 1. Mandatory first action: recover the project state Before changing anything, read these files in order: 1. `.commandcode/BHARATCONTRACT_PROJECT_MEMORY.md` 2. `.commandcode/BHARATCONTRACT_NEXT_SESSION.md` 3. `.commandcode/BHARATCONTRACT_DECISION_LOG.md` 4. `.commandcode/BHARATCONTRACT_ARTIFACT_INDEX.md` 5. `.commandcode/BHARATCONTRACT_SESSION_ARCHIVE.md` Then inspect the current repository state: - Current directory, branch, HEAD commit, and upstream status. - `git status --short --untracked-files=all` - Existing tracked diffs and untracked files. - Relevant current reports in `reports/evaluations/`. - The existing P1 context resolver and P2 evidence-binding implementation. - Relevant tests and application schemas. - The seven outstanding provenance-related test failures. The handoff describes earlier observations. Treat them as leads to verify, not unquestionable facts. ### Protect existing work The repository already contains substantial uncommitted work. - Do not discard, reset, clean, stash, overwrite, or reformat existing work indiscriminately. - Do not assume untracked files are disposable. - Do not overwrite the five newly exported `.commandcode/BHARATCONTRACT_*.md` files. - Do not modify unrelated existing work merely to simplify your task. - Record the initial Git status and HEAD in your task report. - Distinguish pre-existing changes from changes introduced during this mission. - Do not commit, push, amend, rebase, or rewrite Git history. If a proposed change intersects existing modifications, inspect the diff and preserve all existing intent before proceeding. ## 2. Non-negotiable integrity rules These rules override task completion targets. ### No unsupported claims - Never claim a test passed unless you ran it and inspected its exit status and result. - Never claim a defect is fixed without a regression test or another appropriate verification. - Never report a benchmark improvement without an actual, reproducible comparison. - Never infer Indian-law compliance from US-centric CUAD or MAUD datasets. - Never invent legal authorities, quotations, holdings, source URLs, or legal interpretations. - Clearly distinguish observed facts, agent-reported facts, hypotheses, and unverified assumptions. - When you cannot verify something, record it as unverified. ### Preserve provenance and evaluation integrity The existing provenance-related test failures are important and must remain visible. Previously reported full-suite state: - 81 tests collected. - 74 passed. - 7 failed, involving missing or inadequate provenance manifests for existing production artifacts. These counts are historical until independently reproduced. Do not: - Delete or skip these tests. - Weaken assertions to make the suite green. - Add broad exception handlers to conceal failures. - Create fake manifests or fabricate lineage. - Label unverified artifacts as validated. - Swap staged artifacts into production. - Retrain models on held-out data. - Treat text overlap alone as proof of leakage. A legitimate fix is allowed only if it establishes the missing property using truthful, verifiable evidence. Otherwise, document the blocker and preserve the failure. ### Preserve the research baseline Do not modify, regenerate, replace, delete, or extract: - `data/datasets/` - `data/processed/` - `data/processed.staging/` - Existing model weights, archives, or caches. - Production model artifacts. - Existing experiment results or benchmark outputs. Do not run large training jobs, download large datasets, or introduce paid services. No production artifact swap or model retraining is authorized. ## 3. Time budget and execution discipline Use a maximum of 8 hours for productive work. You may continue up to 10 hours only if the environment permits and there is a concrete, safe, high-value task remaining. Do not attempt to keep the process alive artificially. Stop early if remaining tasks require unavailable evidence, infrastructure, or approvals. Use these phases as a planning guide, not as an excuse to fill time: ### Phase A — State recovery and baseline (first 30–60 minutes) - Read the handoff and inspect the repository. - Reproduce the relevant baseline checks. - Run the focused P1 and P2 tests. - Run the full test suite once if practical. - Record actual failures, warnings, skipped tests, and exit codes. - Inspect existing changes before deciding what to edit. ### Phase B — Root-cause investigation (approximately 1–2 hours) Investigate the highest-impact correctness gaps, prioritizing: 1. Whole-contract context and cross-reference handling. 2. Evidence quality and traceability of risk findings. 3. False positives, unsupported claims, and uncertainty handling. 4. Obligation extraction correctness. 5. Missing-protection and internal-inconsistency detection. 6. Provenance and reproducibility safeguards. Read the actual implementations and tests before proposing fixes. Create a short ranked task list with: - Observed failure. - Reproduction steps. - Root cause or explicitly unresolved hypothesis. - Expected benefit. - Risk of regression. - Verification plan. ### Phase C — Targeted engineering improvements (approximately 2–4 hours) Select the highest-value, lowest-risk improvements that can be validated within the available time. Implement only changes supported by the code, tests, and observed behavior. Prefer: - Small deterministic fixes. - Regression tests for genuine defects. - Clear evidence and uncertainty semantics. - Correct handling of missing or ambiguous references. - Improved detection of false positives. - Better handling of clause IDs, offsets, and document-level findings. - Reproducible tests using synthetic contracts. - Explicit abstention when the system lacks enough evidence. Avoid broad architectural changes. ### Phase D — Independent adversarial validation (approximately 1–2 hours) Test the implementation against more than the exact example used to develop it. Build or reuse synthetic contract fixtures covering: - Definitions referenced elsewhere in the contract. - Cross-references and precedence clauses. - Exceptions and carve-outs. - Conflicting provisions. - Schedule overrides. - Explicitly present protections. - Genuinely missing protections. - Ambiguous or unresolved references. - Unrelated keywords that could trigger false positives. - Long clauses and segmented text. - Contract-level findings without a defensible clause locator. - Irrelevant or nonsensical input. - Uncertain legal interpretations. Do not hard-code behavior specifically to one named fixture. Where practical, include positive, negative, and adversarial cases. Ensure tests check both expected findings and findings that should not be produced. Use the existing TC-05 cross-reference diagnostic as one diagnostic fixture, not as the sole evaluation target. Do not tune to a held-out benchmark and then present that same benchmark as independent validation. ### Phase E — Final verification and handoff (final 1–2 hours) - Run focused tests for each changed area. - Run Ruff or the project's existing lint checks. - Run the full suite if practical. - Verify the final diff and Git status. - Review new tests for false confidence, brittle assumptions, or assertions that merely restate the implementation. - Write a report of what was actually accomplished. - Identify the next highest-value task rather than starting an unrelated expansion. ## 4. Specific engineering priorities ### Priority 1: Context-aware contract analysis Inspect `nlp/context/resolver.py`, its tests, and the integration in `app/services/analyzer.py`. The existing resolver is reported to produce reference statuses of `resolved`, `missing`, and `ambiguous`, along with references, overrides, related clause IDs, and unresolved references. Verify: - Whether context is actually consumed by downstream risk rules. - Whether section and schedule references resolve correctly. - Whether unresolved references remain unresolved rather than being silently guessed. - Whether candidate precedence is mistakenly treated as proof of a legal conflict being resolved. - Whether headings, numbering variants, and schedule references cause missed or incorrect associations. Improve downstream behavior only if you can define reliable semantics and prove them through tests. Do not claim that the resolver improves legal accuracy merely because it returns metadata. ### Priority 2: Evidence-backed risk findings Inspect the current `RiskFlag` and `EvidenceSpan` schemas and `_bind_evidence` implementation. Maintain the critical distinction between: - A clause associated with a finding. - A passage that directly supports a factual observation. - A passage that supports a legal proposition. - A model-generated suggestion that has not been verified. - A document-level concern without a defensible local citation. A span covering an entire clause is not proof that the clause supports the associated legal claim. Where practical, make rule findings traceable to the specific matched text and test the offsets against the actual text representation. Preserve correct handling of segmented and cleaned clause text. Do not upgrade an evidence status simply because a span exists. Do not treat uncalibrated model confidence as a probability of legal correctness. ### Priority 3: False positives and missing-protection checks Investigate whether keyword occurrence is incorrectly interpreted as the presence or absence of a contractual protection. A term appearing only in a definition, exception, or unrelated clause may not establish that the protection exists. Conversely, the absence of a keyword does not prove the absence of a protection. Test whole-contract behavior, including exceptions and cross-references. Classify outcomes carefully: - Explicit issue. - Potential issue. - Possible missing protection. - Unclassified or requiring human review. Do not equate commercial disadvantage with illegality. Do not label a missing protection illegal without a verified legal basis. ### Priority 4: Obligation extraction Inspect extraction behavior for: - Actor or responsible party. - Action. - Object. - Trigger or condition. - Deadline. - Exceptions. - Evidence location. A deadline such as “within thirty (30) days” should not be silently dropped when the extractor can reliably identify it. Do not invent an actor, action, or deadline when the contract does not establish one. Use small synthetic fixtures to test precision as well as recall. Avoid expanding extraction scope without a clear evaluation method. ### Priority 5: Provenance and reproducibility Audit the existing provenance guards and artifact manifests. If a safe improvement is possible, make it additive and testable. A manifest must represent real source lineage, actual artifact hashes, and genuine generation details. Keep production artifacts untouched. Do not treat the staged A3 rebuild as production-ready merely because its row-level verifier reportedly passed. Do not claim the previous text-overlap audit establishes a measured leakage rate. It established observed overlap requiring investigation. ## 5. Product and legal-analysis constraints BharatContract AI is intended to help legal professionals and businesses understand contracts and identify review concerns. Maintain these principles: - Neutral bilateral review by default. - Party-focused review only when the represented party is explicitly identified. - Read provisions in their whole-contract context. - Distinguish legal risk from commercial risk. - Distinguish contract text from legal authority and system inference. - Prefer verifiable primary legal sources. - Record jurisdiction, source identity, relevant dates, and verification status when making legal-source claims. - Preserve uncertainty and conflicting evidence. - Do not fabricate legal-source verification. - Do not treat “not found” as “proven absent.” - Do not treat a missing protection as automatically illegal. - Do not claim legal compliance merely because no rule fired. If primary-source verification is unavailable, improve the system's uncertainty handling or document the limitation rather than inventing legal conclusions. ## 6. 216: ## 9. Stages P1 and P2 (implemented, not yet reviewed upstream)
217: 
218: ### P1 — deterministic context resolution
219: `resolve_context(raw_clauses) -> {clause_id: {status, references[], overrides[], related_clause_ids[],
220: unresolved_references[]}}`; reference status `resolved|missing|ambiguous`; precedence recorded as
221: **`candidate` only**. Attached as additive `Clause.context`. **Not consumed by any rule yet.**
222: Known limits: Markdown-prefixed headings (`## 7. LIABILITY`) are not parsed as section numbers, so TC-05
223: references are detected but **unresolved**; `Clause 7.4(a)`, `Section IV`, inline parenthetical
224: definitions unsupported; no inference of precedence from clause order.
225: 
226: ### P2 — evidence binding
227: `EvidenceSpan{text, char_start, char_end, clause_id, role: direct|contextual, locator: "clause_text"}`
228: and five additive `RiskFlag` fields (`source`, `evidence_status`, `evidence_spans`, `search_scope`,
229: `related_clause_ids`). Bound once in `apply_rules` via `_bind_evidence` — **no rule function edited**.
230: - Clause-level → owning clause span, `status="direct"` (**owning-clause association, not proof**).
231: - Contract-level (`clause_id=None`) → **no span**, `status="unverified"`, explicit `search_scope`.
232: - ML → `source="model"`, `status="unverified"`, `role="contextual"`; **confidence is uncalibrated**.
233: - Offsets index cleaned/segmented `Clause.text`, **not** raw file bytes.
234: - Evidence is clause-granular (rules do not expose the matched phrase).

36: Optional JWT auth (`AUTH_ENABLED`, default **off**), bcrypt hashing with a PBKDF2 fallback, ranked roles
37: `viewer < analyst < admin`, `/api/v1/auth/token` + `/me`, owner-scoped reads (404 not 403), case-law pointers
38: per rule, and a weakly-supervised TF-IDF risk classifier used only as a recall booster (`ML_RISK_001`).
39: Commits `316aa5e`, `abef0bd`, `cbd9c29` were made and **pushed**, with explicit approval at the time.
40: 
41: ### Phase 4 — Research-integrity reset
42: A charter and an agent master prompt were supplied. Work switched to a staged protocol: read-only audit →
43: scope → patch proposal → approval → implementation → evaluation. All later work was approval-gated.
44: 
45: ### Phase 5 — Data lineage and leakage
46: CUAD split facts established (510 / 408 / 102; clean partition). The earlier "407/408 mismatch" was
47: identified as a **counting error by the agent**, corrected and recorded. The key finding: the original
48: corpus was built from the **whole** CUADv1, so all 102 held-out documents were inside training.
49: 
50: ### Phase 6 — Provenance subsystem
51: Hash-pinned source allowlist, per-artifact manifests, runtime provenance registry (`/healthz` block,
52: `PROVENANCE_*` tokens in analysis warnings), a fail-closed readiness verifier, and adversarial tests proving a
53: forged manifest cannot rescue an artifact with held-out rows.
54: 
55: ### Phase 7 — A3 backup + staged rebuild
56: Durable backup created; train-only rebuild into `data/processed.staging/` (9,278 classifier rows from 407
57: documents, all `train`); verifier passing on staging; **no production swap**.
58: 
59: ### Phase 8 — Pre-replacement audit
60: Verdict: **NOT READY** for replacement on two procedural grounds (ephemeral backup; verifier ignoring row
61: lineage). Both were then closed: durable backup verified, and row-level lineage added to the verifier.
62: 
63: ### Phase 9 — Keyword-bank behavioural comparison
64: Production vs staged bank, isolated processes, fixed corpus. 308/312 identical; 4 differences; no accuracy
65: claim.
66: 
67: ### Phase 10 — Generalizable analysis audit (Stage A/B)
68: Root causes R1–R9 identified (no cross-reference resolution; single-clause liability rule; evidence-less
69: contract-level findings; keyword-presence missing-protection; unattributed ML findings; obligation field
70: defects; heading inflation; unqualified legal claims). P1→P7 roadmap proposed.
71: 
72: ### Phase 11 — P1 implemented (context resolution)
73: Deterministic resolver added; context attached but **not consumed** by rules. Suite 71/64/7.
74: 
75: ### Phase 12 — P2 implemented (evidence binding)
76: `EvidenceSpan` + five additive `RiskFlag` fields; binding in `apply_rules`; ML findings marked unverified.
77: Suite 81/74/7 with the same seven provenance failures.
78: 
79: ### Phase 13 — This export
80: Documentation only: five handoff files created in `.commandcode/`. No code, test, data, model or artifact
81: change.

1: """Clause segmentation: split a contract into individual clauses.
2: 
3: Two stages:
4:   1. Rule-based heading detection (section numbers, capitalised headings)
5:   2. Sub-paragraph re-segmentation when a 'clause' is still too long.
6: 
7: The output is a list of `Clause` objects with char offsets relative to the
8: full cleaned text.
9: """
10: from __future__ import annotations
11: 
12: import re
13: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
14: from typing import List, Optional
15: 
16: from app.core.logging import get_logger
17: from app.utils.text import (
18:     clean_text,
19:     detect_section_number,
20:     split_into_paragraphs,
21: )
22: 
23: logger = get_logger()
24: 
25: 
26: @dataclass
27: class Clause:
28:     """A logical clause extracted from a contract."""
29: 
30:     clause_id: str
31:     section_number: Optional[str]
32:     heading: Optional[str]
33:     text: str
34:     char_start: int
35:     char_end: int
36:     page_hint: Optional[int] = None
37:     tokens_estimate: int = 0
38:     metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
39: 
40:     @property
41:     def length(self) -> int:
42:         return self.char_end - self.char_start
43: 
44: 
45: # A clause is considered "long" beyond this char count and will be split further.
46: LONG_CLAUSE_CHARS = 2500
47: 
48: 
49: def segment_clauses(
50:     text: str,
51:     *,
52:     contract_id: str,
53:     long_threshold: int = LONG_CLAUSE_CHARS,
54: ) -> List[Clause]:
55:     """Split the full contract text into a list of Clauses.
56: 
57:     Strategy:
58:       * Group paragraphs into clauses based on numbered/heading lines.
59:       * If a clause exceeds long_threshold, fall back to per-paragraph chunks.
60:     """
61:     if not text:
62:         return []
63: 
64:     cleaned = clean_text(text)
65:     if not cleaned:
66:         return []
67: 
68:     paragraphs = split_into_paragraphs(cleaned)
69:     if not paragraphs:
70:         return []
71: 
72:     raw_blocks = _group_paragraphs_into_clauses(paragraphs)
73: 
74:     clauses: List[Clause] = []
75:     cursor = 0
76:     for idx, (heading, section_num, body) in enumerate(raw_blocks, start=1):
77:         full_text = body if not heading else f"{heading}\n\n{body}"
78:         # Find char offsets relative to the entire cleaned text.
79:         start = cleaned.find(full_text[:120], cursor)
80:         if start == -1:
81:             start = cursor
82:         end = start + len(full_text)
83:         cursor = end
84: 
85:         if len(full_text) > long_threshold:
86:             # Split long clause into multiple sub-clauses.
87:             sub_clauses = _split_long_clause(
88:                 body,
89:                 base_id=f"{contract_id}_c{idx:03d}",
90:                 section_number=section_num,
91:                 heading=heading,
92:                 char_start=start,
93:                 long_threshold=long_threshold,
94:             )
95:             for sc in sub_clauses:
96:                 sc.metadata.setdefault("parent_index", idx)
97:             clauses.extend(sub_clauses)
98:         else:
99:             clauses.append(
100:                 Clause(
101:                     clause_id=f"{contract_id}_c{idx:03d}",
102:                     section_number=section_num,
103:                     heading=heading,
104:                     text=full_text.strip(),
105:                     char_start=start,
106:                     char_end=start + len(full_text.strip()),
107:                     tokens_estimate=_estimate_tokens(full_text),
108:                 )
109:             )
110: 
111:     logger.info("Segmented {} clauses (long_threshold={})", len(clauses), long_threshold)
112:     return clauses
113: 
114: 
115: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
116: # Internals
117: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
118: 
119: 
120: def _group_paragraphs_into_clauses(paragraphs: List[str]) -> List[tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], str]]:
121:     """Group paragraphs into (heading, section_number, body) tuples.
122: 
123:     Algorithm:
124:       1. Normalise: split any paragraph that starts with a heading line and
125:          has a body on subsequent lines.
126:       2. Walk through the items. Each time we see a strong-heading line
127:          (starts with a section number OR is an ALL-CAPS legal title),
128:          flush the current buffer as one (heading, body) pair.
129:       3. The first item is special: even if it doesn't match a heading
130:          pattern, we treat it as the preamble's heading so all the
131:          metadata that follows it stays attached as the preamble body.
132:     """
133:     grouped: List[tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], str]] = []
134:     buffer: List[str] = []
135: 
136:     def _trim_heading(h: str) -> Optional[str]:
137:         if not h:
138:             return None
139:         first_line = h.split("\n", 1)[0].strip()
140:         if not first_line:
141:             return None
142:         if len(first_line) > 200:
143:             return None
144:         return first_line
145: 
146:     def flush():
147:         if not buffer:
148:             return
149:         heading_raw = buffer[0]
150:         heading = _trim_heading(heading_raw)
151:         body = "\n\n".join(buffer[1:]) if len(buffer) > 1 else ""
152:         section_num = (
153:             detect_section_number(heading.split("\n", 1)[0]) if heading else None
154:         )
155:         grouped.append((heading, section_num, body))
156:         buffer.clear()
157: 
158:     # Normalise: a heading + body joined by a single newline should be split.
159:     normalised: List[str] = []
160:     for p in paragraphs:
161:         lines = p.split("\n")
162:         first = lines[0].strip()
163:         rest = "\n".join(lines[1:]).strip()
164:         if _looks_like_heading_line(first) and rest:
165:             normalised.append(first)
166:             normalised.append(rest)
167:         else:
168:             normalised.append(p)
169: 
170:     for idx, para in enumerate(normalised):
171:         first_line = para.split("\n", 1)[0].strip()
172:         # Strong heading only — not every numbered body paragraph.
173:         is_strong_heading = _looks_like_heading_line(first_line)
174:         if idx == 0 and not buffer:
175:             # Force-start the first group with whatever we see.
176:             buffer.append(para)
177:         elif is_strong_heading:
178:             flush()
179:             buffer.append(para)
180:         else:
181:             buffer.append(para)
182:     flush()
183: 
184:     if not grouped:
185:         grouped = [(None, None, p) for p in paragraphs]
186: 
187:     return grouped
188: 
189: 
190: def _looks_like_heading_line(line: str) -> bool:
191:     """Return True if a single line looks like a clause heading.
192: 
193:     Heuristic is intentionally strict to avoid false positives on body text.
194:     A line qualifies only if it has either a section number or it is short,
195:     ALL-CAPS and has no terminal punctuation.
196:     """
197:     if not line:
198:         return False
199:     if len(line) > 120:
200:         return False
201:     # Section number ("1.", "1.1", "(a)", "Article 5", etc.). Numbered body
202:     # sentences also match this regex, so reject terminal punctuation and
203:     # long lines; those are clause text, not headings.
204:     if detect_section_number(line):
205:         stripped = line.strip()
206:         if stripped.endswith((".", ",", ";", ":")):
207:             return False
208:         return len(stripped.split()) <= 12
209:     stripped = line.strip()
210:     # Strip out parenthetical / quoted segments before checking case so
211:     # 'RESIDENT ACCOMMODATION SERVICE AGREEMENT ("Agreement")' is treated as
212:     # an all-caps heading.
213:     cleaned = re.sub(r"\([^)]*\)", "", stripped)
214:     cleaned = re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', "", cleaned)
215:     cleaned = re.sub(r"'[^']*'", "", cleaned).strip()
216:     has_alpha = any(c.isalpha() for c in cleaned)
217:     if (
218:         has_alpha
219:         and cleaned == cleaned.upper()
220:         and len(stripped) <= 120
221:         and not stripped.endswith(".")
222:         and not stripped.endswith(",")
223:     ):
224:         return True
225:     # Keyword hint — only if the line is very short (<= 60 chars) and is title-cased.
226:     if (
227:         len(stripped) <= 60
228:         and not stripped.endswith(".")
229:         and not stripped.endswith(",")
230:         and not any(c.isdigit() for c in stripped)
231:         and stripped == stripped.title()
232:         and any(t in stripped.lower() for t in _HEADING_HINTS)
233:     ):
234:         return True
235:     return False
236: 
237: 
238: _HEADING_HINTS = (
239:     "indemnif",
240:     "liability",
241:     "termination",
242:     "payment",
243:     "confidential",

245:     "intellectual property",

274: def _split_long_clause(
275:     body: str,
276:     *,
277:     base_id: str,
278:     section_number: Optional[str],
279:     heading: Optional[str],
280:     char_start: int,
281:     long_threshold: int = LONG_CLAUSE_CHARS,
282: ) -> List[Clause]:
283:     """Split a clause body into smaller pieces at paragraph or sentence
284:     boundaries.
285: 
286:     Three-stage strategy:
287:       1. Group paragraphs into chunks <= long_threshold.
288:       2. If a single paragraph is still larger than the threshold, split it
289:          by sentence boundaries (`.!?`).
290:       3. As a last resort, perform a fixed-character split.
291:     """
292:     paragraphs = split_into_paragraphs(body)
293:     clauses: List[Clause] = []
294:     buffer: List[str] = []
295:     buffer_len = 0
296:     sub_idx = 1
297: 
298:     def flush():
299:         nonlocal sub_idx, buffer_len
300:         if not buffer:
301:             return
302:         joined = "\n\n".join(buffer).strip()
303:         clause_id = f"{base_id}_s{sub_idx:02d}"
304:         prior_len = sum(len(c.text) + 2 for c in clauses)
305:         local_start = char_start + prior_len
306:         clauses.append(
307:             Clause(
308:                 clause_id=clause_id,
309:                 section_number=section_number,
310:                 heading=heading,
311:                 text=joined,
312:                 char_start=local_start,
313:                 char_end=local_start + len(joined),
314:                 tokens_estimate=_estimate_tokens(joined),
315:                 metadata={"split": True, "sub_index": sub_idx},
316:             )
317:         )
318:         sub_idx += 1
319:         buffer.clear()
320:         buffer_len = 0
321: 
322:     def _split_oversized_paragraph(p: str) -> List[str]:
323:         """Split a single oversized paragraph into sentence-sized chunks."""
324:         if len(p) <= long_threshold:
325:             return [p]
326:         # Stage 2: sentence split
327:         sentence_chunks = [s for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", p) if s.strip()]
328:         # Stage 3: fixed-char split if a sentence alone exceeds threshold
329:         out: List[str] = []
330:         for s in sentence_chunks:
331:             if len(s) <= long_threshold:
332:                 out.append(s)
333:                 continue
334:             for i in range(0, len(s), long_threshold):
335:                 out.append(s[i : i + long_threshold])
336:         return out or [p]
337: 
338:     expanded: List[str] = []
339:     for p in paragraphs:
340:         if len(p) > long_threshold:
341:             expanded.extend(_split_oversized_paragraph(p))
342:         else:
343:             expanded.append(p)
344: 
345:     for p in expanded:
346:         if buffer_len + len(p) > long_threshold and buffer:
347:             flush()
348:         buffer.append(p)
349:         buffer_len += len(p)
350:     flush()
351:     return clauses
352: 
353: 
354: _TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\S+")
355: 
356: 
357: def _estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
358:     """Rough token estimate (avg 4 chars per token for English)."""
359:     return max(1, len(text) // 4)

1: """Text cleaning and normalisation utilities used across the pipeline."""
2: from __future__ import annotations
3: 
4: import re
5: import unicodedata
6: from typing import List
7: 
8: # Whitespace normalisation regexes
9: _WS_RE = re.compile(r"[ \t\f\v]+")
10: _NL_RE = re.compile(r"\n{3,}")
11: _CONTROL_RE = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]")
12: 
13: # Smart quote mapping (preserve readability while keeping tokens stable)
14: _SMART_QUOTE_MAP = str.maketrans({
15:     "\u2018": "'", "\u2019": "'",
16:     "\u201c": '"', "\u201d": '"',
17:     "\u2013": "-", "\u2014": "-",
18:     "\u2026": "...",
19: })
20: 
21: # Common Indian legal abbreviations and their expansions (used in token-pass hint).
22: INDIAN_LEGAL_TERMS = {
23:     "MSA": "Master Services Agreement",
24:     "NDA": "Non-Disclosure Agreement",
25:     "SPA": "Share Purchase Agreement",
26:     "SHA": "Shareholders Agreement",
27:     "CIN": "Corporate Identity Number",
28:     "PAN": "Permanent Account Number",
29:     "GSTIN": "Goods and Services Tax Identification Number",
30:     "TDS": "Tax Deducted at Source",
31:     "FY": "Financial Year",
32:     "INR": "Indian Rupee",
33: }
34: 
35: 
36: def normalise_whitespace(text: str) -> str:
37:     """Collapse runs of whitespace and trim each line, while preserving
38:     paragraph breaks (consecutive blank lines)."""
39:     if not text:
40:         return ""
41:     text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
42:     text = _CONTROL_RE.sub("", text)
43:     cleaned_lines: list[str] = []
44:     blanks = 0
45:     for line in text.split("\n"):
46:         normalised = _WS_RE.sub(" ", line).strip()
47:         if not normalised:
48:             blanks += 1
49:             continue
50:         if blanks > 0 and cleaned_lines:
51:             # separator — keep as a single blank line between paragraphs.
52:             cleaned_lines.append("")
53:         cleaned_lines.append(normalised)
54:         blanks = 0
55:     return _NL_RE.sub("\n\n", "\n".join(cleaned_lines)).strip()
56: 
57: 
58: def normalise_unicode(text: str) -> str:
59:     """Normalise smart quotes, dashes, ellipsis to ASCII equivalents."""
60:     if not text:
61:         return ""
62:     text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
63:     return text.translate(_SMART_QUOTE_MAP)
64: 
65: 
66: def clean_text(text: str) -> str:
67:     """Full cleaning pipeline: unicode -> whitespace."""
68:     if not text:
69:         return ""
70:     return normalise_whitespace(normalise_unicode(text))
71: 
72: 
73: _SECTION_HEADING_RE = re.compile(
74:     r"""^(?P<num>
75:         (?:\d+(?:\.\d+)*)            # 1, 1.1, 1.1.1
76:         |(?:[A-Z]\.)                 # A.
77:         |(?:\([a-z0-9]+\))           # (a), (1)
78:         |(?:Article\s+\d+)           # Article 5
79:     )[\.\):]?\s+(?P<heading>.+)$""",
80:     re.VERBOSE,
81: )
82: 
83: 
84: def looks_like_section_heading(line: str) -> bool:
85:     """Heuristic check: does this line look like a clause heading?"""
86:     if not line:
87:         return False
88:     if len(line) > 180:
89:         return False
90:     return bool(_SECTION_HEADING_RE.match(line.strip()))
91: 
92: 
93: def detect_section_number(line: str) -> str | None:
94:     """Extract the section number if present, else None."""
95:     if not line:
96:         return None
97:     match = _SECTION_HEADING_RE.match(line.strip())
98:     return match.group("num") if match else None
99: 
100: 
101: def split_into_paragraphs(text: str) -> List[str]:
102:     """Split cleaned text into non-empty paragraphs."""
103:     if not text:
104:         return []
105:     return [p.strip() for p in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", text) if p.strip()]

1: """Deterministic cross-reference / context resolution for contract clauses.
2: 
3: Scope (deliberately narrow):
4:   * find references to clauses/sections/schedules/exhibits/annexures/appendices;
5:   * resolve them against the *current document's* parsed structure;
6:   * resolve defined terms (``"Term" means ...``) across clauses;
7:   * record explicit precedence/override language as a **candidate**, never as proof
8:     that a conflict is resolved;
9:   * report unresolved / ambiguous / missing references.
10: 
11: Nothing here decides legal meaning. The existing risk rules are untouched: this
12: module only produces a traceable context bundle for each clause.
13: """
14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: import re
17: from typing import Dict, Iterable, List
18: 
19: STATUS_RESOLVED = "resolved"
20: STATUS_MISSING = "missing"
21: STATUS_AMBIGUOUS = "ambiguous"
22: STATUS_CANDIDATE = "candidate"  # precedence language that references something
23: BUNDLE_COMPLETE = "complete"
24: BUNDLE_PARTIAL = "partial"
25: BUNDLE_NONE = "none"
26: 
27: _REF_RE = re.compile(
28:     r"\b(?P<kind>clauses?|sections?|schedules?|exhibits?|annexures?|appendices|appendix)"
29:     r"\s+(?P<nums>\d+(?:\.\d+)*(?:\s*(?:,|and|or|&|to)\s*\d+(?:\.\d+)*)*)",
30:     re.IGNORECASE,
31: )
32: _DEF_RE = re.compile(
33:     r"[\"\u201c](?P<term>[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 ,/&'\-]{1,60}?)[\"\u201d]\s*(?:means|shall mean|refers to|has the meaning)",
34:     re.IGNORECASE,
35: )
36: _PRECEDENCE_RE = re.compile(
37:     r"\b(notwithstanding|prevails?|shall prevail|subject to|overrid(?:e|es|ing|den))\b",
38:     re.IGNORECASE,
39: )
40: _SCHEDULE_HEAD_RE = re.compile(
41:     r"^\s*#*\s*(?P<kind>schedule|exhibit|annexure|appendix)\s+(?P<key>[A-Za-z0-9]+)", re.IGNORECASE
42: )
43: _NUM_RE = re.compile(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)*")
44: _SENTENCE_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=[.;:])\s+|\n+")
45: 
46: 
47: def _norm_key(value: str) -> str:
48:     return re.sub(r"\s+", "", (value or "").strip().lower())
49: 
50: 
51: def _sentences(text: str) -> List[str]:
52:     return [s.strip() for s in _SENTENCE_RE.split(text or "") if s and s.strip()]
53: 
54: 
55: def _build_indexes(clauses: Iterable) -> dict:
56:     by_section: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
57:     by_sched: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
58:     definitions: Dict[str, dict] = {}
59:     for cl in clauses:
60:         cid = getattr(cl, "clause_id", None)
61:         if not cid:
62:             continue
63:         sec = getattr(cl, "section_number", None)
64:         if sec:
65:             by_section.setdefault(_norm_key(sec), []).append(cid)
66:         head = getattr(cl, "heading", None) or ""
67:         m = _SCHEDULE_HEAD_RE.match(head)
68:         if m:
69:             by_sched.setdefault(_norm_key(m.group("key")), []).append(cid)
70:         for dm in _DEF_RE.finditer(getattr(cl, "text", "") or ""):
71:             term = _norm_key(dm.group("term"))
72:             if term and term not in definitions:
73:                 definitions[term] = {"term": dm.group("term").strip(), "clause_id": cid}
74:     return {"by_section": by_section, "by_sched": by_sched, "definitions": definitions}
75: 
76: 
77: def _targets(kind: str, nums: str, idx: dict) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
78:     """Resolve one reference group; returns (clause_ids, status)."""
79:     kind = kind.lower()
80:     keys = [_norm_key(n) for n in _NUM_RE.findall(nums or "")]
81:     if not keys:
82:         return [], STATUS_MISSING
83:     resolved: List[str] = []
84:     status = STATUS_RESOLVED
85:     for key in keys:
86:         if kind.startswith(("schedule", "exhibit", "annex", "appendix")):
87:             found = idx["by_sched"].get(key, [])
88:         else:
89:             found = idx["by_section"].get(key, [])
90:         if not found:
91:             status = STATUS_MISSING
92:             continue
93:         if len(found) > 1:
94:             status = STATUS_AMBIGUOUS
95:             resolved.extend(found)
96:             continue
97:         resolved.extend(found)
98:     return sorted(set(resolved)), status
99: 
100: 
101: def resolve_context(clauses: Iterable) -> Dict[str, dict]:
102:     """Return ``{clause_id: context_bundle}`` for every clause in the document."""
103:     clauses = list(clauses)
104:     idx = _build_indexes(clauses)
105:     bundles: Dict[str, dict] = {}
106: 
107:     for cl in clauses:
108:         cid = getattr(cl, "clause_id", None)
109:         if not cid:
110:             continue
111:         text = getattr(cl, "text", "") or ""
112:         references: List[dict] = []
113:         overrides: List[dict] = []
114:         unresolved: List[str] = []
115:         related: set[str] = set()
116: 
117:         for m in _REF_RE.finditer(text):
118:             raw = " ".join(m.group(0).split())
119:             targets, status = _targets(m.group("kind"), m.group("nums"), idx)
120:             targets = [t for t in targets if t != cid]
121:             references.append(
122:                 {
123:                     "raw": raw,
124:                     "kind": m.group("kind").lower().rstrip("s"),
125:                     "target_clause_ids": targets,
126:                     "status": status,
127:                 }
128:             )
129:             if status == STATUS_RESOLVED and targets:
130:                 related.update(targets)
131:             else:
132:                 unresolved.append(raw)
133: 
134:         # Defined terms used in this clause (whole-term match, case-insensitive).
135:         for _term, meta in idx["definitions"].items():
136:             if meta["clause_id"] == cid:
137:                 continue
138:             if re.search(r"(?<![a-z0-9])" + re.escape(meta["term"]).lower() + r"(?![a-z0-9])", text.lower()):
139:                 references.append(
140:                     {
141:                         "raw": meta["term"],
142:                         "kind": "definition",
143:                         "target_clause_ids": [meta["clause_id"]],
144:                         "status": STATUS_RESOLVED,
145:                     }
146:                 )
147:                 related.add(meta["clause_id"])
148: 
149:         # Precedence language is recorded as a CANDIDATE only - never as proof.
150:         for sentence in _sentences(text):
151:             if not _PRECEDENCE_RE.search(sentence):
152:                 continue
153:             for ref in [r for r in references if r["target_clause_ids"]]:
154:                 if ref["raw"] in sentence:
155:                     overrides.append(
156:                         {
157:                             "raw": " ".join(sentence.split())[:240],
158:                             "marker": _PRECEDENCE_RE.search(sentence).group(0).lower(),
159:                             "target_clause_ids": ref["target_clause_ids"],
160:                             "status": STATUS_CANDIDATE,
161:                         }
162:                     )
163: 
164:         if references or overrides:
165:             status = BUNDLE_PARTIAL if unresolved else BUNDLE_COMPLETE
166:         else:
167:             status = BUNDLE_NONE
168: 
169:         bundles[cid] = {
170:             "status": status,
171:             "references": references,
172:             "overrides": overrides,
173:             "related_clause_ids": sorted(related),
174:             "unresolved_references": unresolved,
175:         }
176:     return bundles

1: """Obligation extraction using spaCy dependency patterns + regex.
2: 
3: This module emits structured Obligation objects for every detected duty,
4: right, prohibition, or conditional clause. It is deliberately rule-based
5: to remain explainable and fast on the MVP; an LLM-based extractor can
6: augment this in a later phase.
7: """
8: from __future__ import annotations
9: 
10: import re
11: from dataclasses import dataclass
12: from typing import List, Optional
13: 
14: from app.models.schemas import Obligation, ObligationType, RiskSeverity
15: 
16: # Modal patterns are checked in priority order: prohibition, right, obligation.
17: _DEONTIC_PATTERNS = (
18:     (
19:         ObligationType.PROHIBITION,
20:         re.compile(
21:             r"\b(?:shall|may|must|will)\s+not\b|\bis\s+prohibited\s+from\b",
22:             re.IGNORECASE,
23:         ),
24:     ),
25:     (
26:         ObligationType.RIGHT,
27:         re.compile(
28:             r"\b(?:is\s+entitled\s+to|has\s+the\s+right\s+to|reserves\s+the\s+right\s+to)\b"
29:             r"|\b(?:may|can)\b",
30:             re.IGNORECASE,
31:         ),
32:     ),
33:     (
34:         ObligationType.OBLIGATION,
35:         re.compile(
36:             r"\b(?:agrees\s+to|is\s+required\s+to|undertakes\s+to)\b|\b(?:shall|must|will)\b",
37:             re.IGNORECASE,
38:         ),
39:     ),
40: )
41: 
42: DEADLINE_RE = re.compile(
43:     r"\b(?:within|no later than|at least|prior to|after|by|on)\s+"
44:     r"(\d+\s+(?:hour|hours|day|days|week|weeks|month|months|year|years|business\s+days))\b",
45:     re.IGNORECASE,
46: )
47: DATE_DEADLINE_RE = re.compile(
48:     r"\b(?:on\s+or\s+before|by|on|before|after)\s+"
49:     r"(\d{1,2}\s+(?:january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|december)\s+\d{4})\b",
50:     re.IGNORECASE,
51: )
52: 
53: OBJECT_CUT_RE = re.compile(
54:     r"\b(?:within|by|no\s+later\s+than|prior\s+to|on\s+or\s+before|if|unless|subject\s+to|"
55:     r"pursuant\s+to|under\s+this|in\s+accordance\s+with)\b|[.;]",
56:     re.IGNORECASE,
57: )
58: 
59: CONDITIONAL_RE = re.compile(
60:     r"\b(if|provided that|subject to|unless|upon|in case|where)\b", re.IGNORECASE
61: )
62: 
63: 
64: @dataclass
65: class ObligationHit:
66:     text: str
67:     obligation_type: ObligationType
68:     subject: Optional[str]
69:     counterparty: Optional[str]
70:     action: Optional[str]
71:     object: Optional[str]
72:     condition: Optional[str]
73:     deadline_expression: Optional[str]
74:     deadline_date: Optional[str]
75:     risk_level: RiskSeverity
76:     confidence: float
77: 
78: 
79: def extract_obligations_from_clause(
80:     clause_id: str,
81:     clause_text: str,
82:     *,
83:     obligation_counter: int = 0,
84: ) -> list:
85:     """Parse a clause into structured Obligation rows."""
86:     if not clause_text or not clause_text.strip():
87:         return []
88: 
89:     # Split by sentence-like boundaries while keeping them in order
90:     sentences = _split_sentences(clause_text)
91:     obligations: list = []
92:     for sent in sentences:
93:         hit = _analyse_sentence(sent)
94:         if not hit:
95:             continue
96:         obligation_counter += 1
97:         obligations.append(
98:             Obligation(
99:                 obligation_id=f"{clause_id}_obg{obligation_counter:03d}",
100:                 clause_id=clause_id,
101:                 text=sent.strip(),
102:                 obligation_type=hit.obligation_type,
103:                 subject=hit.subject,
104:                 counterparty=hit.counterparty,
105:                 action=hit.action,
106:                 object=hit.object,
107:                 condition=hit.condition,
108:                 deadline_expression=hit.deadline_expression,
109:                 deadline_date=hit.deadline_date,
110:                 risk_level=hit.risk_level,
111:                 confidence=hit.confidence,
112:                 source="rule",
113:             )
114:         )
115:     return obligations
116: 
117: 
118: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
119: # Internals
120: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
121: 
122: 
123: def _split_sentences(text: str) -> List[str]:
124:     """Sentence splitter that respects legal abbreviations and headings."""
125:     # First, split on double-newlines / headings.
126:     # Strip the leading heading-like prefix (e.g. "1. Limitation of Liability").
127:     text = re.sub(r"^\s*\d+(?:\.\d+)*\.?\s+[A-Z][^\n]{0,120}\n", "", text, count=1)
128:     # Normalise whitespace but keep newlines as sentence boundaries for now.
129:     text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text).strip()
130:     text = re.sub(r"\n+", " ", text)
131:     # Protect common abbreviations
132:     placeholders = {
133:         "Pvt.": "Pvt\u0001",
134:         "Ltd.": "Ltd\u0001",
135:         "Inc.": "Inc\u0001",
136:         "Corp.": "Corp\u0001",
137:         "Co.": "Co\u0001",
138:         "Mr.": "Mr\u0001",
139:         "Ms.": "Ms\u0001",
140:         "Mrs.": "Mrs\u0001",
141:         "Dr.": "Dr\u0001",
142:         "No.": "No\u0001",
143:         "vs.": "vs\u0001",
144:         "etc.": "etc\u0001",
145:         "i.e.": "i\u0001e\u0001",
146:         "e.g.": "e\u0001g\u0001",
147:     }
148:     for k, v in placeholders.items():
149:         text = text.replace(k, v)
150:     parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", text)
151:     sentences = []
152:     for p in parts:
153:         for k, v in placeholders.items():
154:             p = p.replace(v, k)
155:         if p.strip():
156:             sentences.append(p.strip())
157:     return sentences
158: 
159: 
160: def _analyse_sentence(sentence: str) -> Optional[ObligationHit]:
161:     sentence = sentence.strip()
162:     if not sentence:
163:         return None
164: 
165:     obligation_type: Optional[ObligationType] = None
166:     modal_match: Optional[re.Match] = None
167:     for candidate_type, pattern in _DEONTIC_PATTERNS:
168:         match = pattern.search(sentence)
169:         if match:
170:             obligation_type = candidate_type
171:             modal_match = match
172:             break
173:     if obligation_type is None or modal_match is None:
174:         return None
175: 
176:     confidence = {
177:         ObligationType.OBLIGATION: 0.85,
178:         ObligationType.RIGHT: 0.7,
179:         ObligationType.PROHIBITION: 0.8,
180:     }[obligation_type]
181: 
182:     # The subject belongs to the first deontic verb, even when the sentence
183:     # later contains a prohibition ("shall keep ... and shall not disclose").
184:     first_modal_start = min(
185:         (match.start() for _, pattern in _DEONTIC_PATTERNS if (match := pattern.search(sentence))),
186:         default=modal_match.start(),
187:     )
188:     subject = _extract_subject(sentence[:first_modal_start])
189:     raw_tail = sentence[modal_match.end() :].strip()
190:     if re.match(r"be\s+", raw_tail, re.IGNORECASE) and re.search(
191:         r"\b(seat|venue)\b", subject or "", re.IGNORECASE
192:     ):
193:         return None
194:     action, obj = _extract_action_object(raw_tail)
195:     if action == "governed":
196:         return None
197:     if action == "resolved" and subject and re.search(r"\b(seat|venue|dispute)\b", subject):
198:         return None
199:     condition = _extract_condition(sentence)
200:     deadline_expr = _extract_deadline(sentence)
201:     risk_level = _derive_risk_level(obligation_type, deadline_expr, sentence.lower())
202: 
203:     return ObligationHit(
204:         text=sentence,
205:         obligation_type=obligation_type,
206:         subject=subject,
207:         counterparty=None,
208:         action=action,
209:         object=obj,
210:         condition=condition,
211:         deadline_expression=deadline_expr,
212:         deadline_date=None,
213:         risk_level=risk_level,
214:         confidence=confidence,
215:     )
216: 
217: 
218: def _extract_subject(prefix: str) -> Optional[str]:
219:     subject = re.sub(r"^\s*\(?[a-z0-9]+[.)]\s*", "", prefix)
220:     subject = re.sub(r"^\s*\d+(?:\.\d+)*\.?\s+", "", subject)
221:     subject = re.sub(
222:         r"^(?:thereafter|however|notwithstanding(?:\s+the\s+foregoing)?|further|additionally)\s+",
223:         "",
224:         subject.strip(),
225:         flags=re.IGNORECASE,
226:     )
227:     subject = subject.strip().rstrip(",;:")
228:     if len(subject) > 100:
229:         subject = re.split(r"[,;]", subject)[-1].strip()
230:     subject = re.sub(r"^(?:the|this|that|a|an)\s+", "", subject, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
231:     subject = re.sub(r"\s+(?:to|of|from|in|under|pursuant|for|by)\s*$", "", subject)
232:     subject = subject.strip().rstrip(",;:")
233:     if len(subject) < 2:
234:         return None
235:     return subject[:120]
236: 
237: 
238: def _extract_action_object(rest: str) -> tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str]]:
239:     rest = rest.strip().lstrip(",;: ")
240:     rest = re.sub(r"^(?:not|hereby|also)\s+", "", rest, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
241:     unlimited = re.match(r"have\s+(unlimited|no|full)\s+liability\b", rest, re.IGNORECASE)
242:     if unlimited:
243:         return "bear", f"{unlimited.group(1).lower()} liability{rest[unlimited.end():]}".strip()
244:     rest = re.sub(r"^(?:be|have)\s+", "", rest, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
245:     if not rest:
246:         return None, None
247:

The `_analyse_sentence` returns an ObligationHit with `deadline_expression=None`. But my DEADLINE_RE should match "within thirty (30) days". Let me check why it didn't match. The deadline regex: `\b(?:within|...)\s+(thirty|...)\)?\s+(?:hour|...|days)`. "within thirty (30) days" → "within " then "thirty" then " " then "(" ... wait, after "thirty" comes " (30) days". So `\s+` after the number word expects whitespace then unit, but there's " (30)" in between. My regex `\)?` only allows one optional ")" right after the number, not "(30)". 

So "thirty (30) days" doesn't match because between "thirty" and "days" there's "(30)". 

I need to allow an optional parenthetical number between the number word and the unit: `(?:\s*\(\d+\))?`. Let me update DEADLINE_RE number group.

/arbor # BharatContract AI — Unattended Autonomous Work Mode ## Operating instruction You are authorized to work autonomously in the existing BharatContract AI repository while I am away from my desk. Use the Arbor skill and Beam 1.0. Continue making useful, independently verifiable progress without asking me to approve every routine step. **Maximum runtime: 8 hours. Absolute ceiling: 10 hours if the environment supports it.** These are limits, not targets. Never wait idly or invent tasks to consume time. Do not depend on receiving another user message. Maintain a durable record of progress so the work can be resumed if the model, terminal, or session stops. ## 1. Recover and protect the repository Read the five `.commandcode/BHARATCONTRACT_*.md` handoff files and the existing session log. Inspect the actual Git branch, HEAD, worktree, and diffs. Preserve all existing modifications, untracked files, research artifacts, and the two fixes already reported in `app/utils/text.py` and `nlp/obligation_extraction/extractor.py`. Never run destructive Git commands. Never stage, commit, push, amend, rebase, or rewrite history. Do not overwrite existing reports or handoff files. Check each proposed output path first. ## 2. Work autonomously in this order Complete each task as far as evidence allows. After finishing or blocking a task, record its result and proceed to the next safe, useful task. ### Task A — P4: Context-aware liability and renewal rules - Inspect and reproduce existing false positives. - Integrate the P1 context bundle into liability and renewal rules where semantically justified. - Test genuine concerns as well as false positives. - Cover definitions, caps, exceptions, precedence, renewal opt-outs, reminders, and unresolved references. - Use multiple synthetic contracts and varied wording. - Do not hard-code TC-05 clause IDs or wording. - Do not treat a resolved reference as proof that one provision overrides another. - Do not silently suppress findings when context is ambiguous. If the integration cannot be made reliable, document the blocker and move to the next task. ### Task B — Generalize regression coverage Inspect the current tests for: - Markdown headings and section references. - Written-out deadlines and parenthetical digits. - Context resolution. - Evidence binding. - Contract-level findings. - Obligation extraction. - False positives caused by keywords appearing in definitions or unrelated clauses. Add only high-value tests for demonstrated gaps. Test negative cases as well as positive ones. Avoid duplicating existing tests or overfitting one fixture. ### Task C — Evidence and finding integrity Audit the risk-finding pipeline for cases where: - A whole-clause span is presented as if it proves a legal claim. - A contract-level finding lacks a defensible clause locator. - Model-generated suggestions appear verified despite being unverified. - Uncalibrated confidence is treated as legal certainty. - A missing keyword is interpreted as proof that a protection is absent. - A rule's failure to fire is interpreted as proof that a contract is safe. Fix small, clearly established defects only. Preserve the existing meaning of evidence-status fields unless a justified, tested change is essential. ### Task D — Obligation extraction Investigate whether actors, actions, triggers, exceptions, and deadlines are extracted correctly. Use small synthetic examples, including ambiguous obligations and written-out dates or durations. Avoid inventing missing information. Measure precision-related false positives as well as missed obligations. ### Task E — Provenance and reproducibility audit Inspect the seven known provenance failures and their corresponding guards. Do not manufacture lineage, hashes, or manifests. Do not replace production artifacts. Fix a provenance issue only when its underlying cause can be genuinely resolved and independently verified. If the only safe action is to document the missing provenance, do that and move on. ### Task F — Final integration and review Review the complete diff, run the available verification commands, check for regressions, and create a final report. If the tasks above are completed, identify another concrete, low-risk correctness defect in the existing implementation. Reproduce it, add a regression test, make a minimal fix, and verify it before proceeding. Do not invent additional architecture, features, or work merely to keep busy. ## 3. Verification protocol Use the project's existing `uv` environment. Run the relevant focused tests and lint checks after each change. Run the full suite at baseline and at the end when practical. At minimum, attempt these commands when appropriate: - `uv run --no-sync ruff check .` - `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_context_resolution.py -q` - `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_evidence_binding.py -q` - `uv run --no-sync pytest -q` Capture actual exit codes and results. Do not assume the earlier test counts are current. The last reported full-suite state was 76 passed and 7 failed out of 81 collected. The seven provenance failures were T1a, T1b, T2a, T2b, T3a, T3b, and T8. Reproduce this baseline before relying on it. Never hide failures, weaken tests to make the suite green, or claim success from incomplete output. For every implemented fix, record: 1. Reproduced defect. 2. Root cause established from code. 3. Files changed. 4. Regression test. 5. Verification command and actual result. 6. Remaining limitations. ## 4. Strictly prohibited actions Without further user authorization, do not: - Modify, delete, regenerate, or replace anything in `data/datasets/`, `data/processed/`, or `data/processed.staging/`. - Retrain models, replace model weights, extract archives, or change production artifacts. - Download large datasets or models. - Install heavyweight dependencies or paid services. - Start external services or infrastructure without a demonstrated need. - Modify unrelated frontend, deployment, or configuration components. - Perform network publication, external uploads, or other consequential external actions. - Commit or push changes. - Overwrite existing user files, reports, or handoff records. Keep the existing seven provenance failures visible unless their actual causes are truthfully fixed. ## 5. Durable progress tracking Create a new progress log under `.commandcode/`, using a filename that does not already exist. Record: - Initial HEAD and worktree state. - Task currently being attempted. - Tasks completed and their evidence. - Files changed. - Tests run and their actual results. - Known failures and blockers. - The exact next action if interrupted. Update this log after each completed task or meaningful milestone, not after every tiny command. Create a new final report under `reports/evaluations/`, checking that the path does not already exist. Include verified changes, tests, remaining failures, and limitations. Never overwrite the existing handoff export or previous evaluation reports. ## 6. Recovery and context management If context is running low, stop starting new tasks. First save the current state, exact next steps, test results, and unresolved questions to the progress log. If the environment restarts or the conversation context is lost, recover from the durable log and repository state before resuming. Do not assume previous work succeeded merely because the log says it was attempted; verify the relevant files and tests. If subagents are available, use them selectively for independent test design or diff review. Do not allow concurrent agents to edit the same files. ## 7. Stop conditions Stop when: - The runtime ceiling is reached. - No further meaningful, safely verifiable task remains. - Required evidence or infrastructure is unavailable. - A change risks losing user work or modifying protected artifacts. - A genuine authorization boundary is encountered. Do not ask me questions for routine decisions covered by this instruction. Choose the safest reversible option, document uncertainty, and continue with another independent task when appropriate. ## 8. Final report At the end, report: - What actually improved. - Files changed. - Focused and full-suite test results. - Whether the seven provenance failures remain. - Whether production data and models remained untouched. - Any remaining limitations. - Final Git status, including pre-existing modifications. - The single highest-value next action. Do not commit or push. **Start now. Work unattended through the task sequence, save progress durably, verify every claimed fix, and stop safely when finished or blocked.**

370:     summary: ContractSummary,
371: ) -> List[RiskFlag]:
372:     """Run all registered rules against every clause. Returns a flat list.
373: 
374:     Rules with `is_contract_level=True` run once at the contract level and are
375:     NOT duplicated per clause. All other rules may fire per-clause; we then
376:     dedupe by rule_id keeping the highest-severity occurrence so the UI does
377:     not show the same rule three times for three matching clauses.
378:     """
379:     raw_flags: List[RiskFlag] = []
380: 
381:     # 1. Per-clause rules
382:     for cl in clauses:
383:         for rule in RISK_RULES:
384:             if rule.is_contract_level:
385:                 continue
386:             if rule.requires_indian and (
387:                 not summary.jurisdiction or summary.jurisdiction.lower() not in {"india", "indian"}

389:                 continue
390:             try:
391:                 flag = rule.check(cl, summary) if rule.check else None
392:             except Exception:
393:                 continue
394:             if flag:
395:                 raw_flags.append(flag)

397:     # 2. Contract-level rules
398:     raw_flags.extend(_contract_level_rules(clauses, summary))

Now I understand the structure. The P4 task wants me to integrate context into liability/renewal rules. The context bundle is attached to `Clause.context` (a dict). The liability rule `rule_uncapped_liability` checks if a single clause has cap language. The false positive `RISK_LIABILITY_002` fires when a Limitation-of-Liability clause lacks cap language AND no payment amount entity. But if a related clause (referenced via context) contains cap language, the finding should be suppressed.

The challenge: rules only see one clause at a time. To check related clauses, I'd need access to all clauses or the context bundle's related_clause_ids. The Clause has `.context` attribute with `related_clause_ids`. But the rule doesn't have access to the full clause list or their text.

Approach: In `apply_rules`, I could pre-compute a map of clause_id → Clause, and pass it to rules. But rules are called as `rule.check(cl, summary)`. Changing the signature would break the RiskRule contract.

Alternative: store the related clause texts in the Clause's context bundle? No, context only has IDs.

Alternative: Make `rule_uncapped_liability` look up related clauses from a module-level or passed-in registry. 

Actually, the cleanest minimal change: in `apply_rules`, before running rules, attach a helper. But rules are plain functions.

98: def _analyse(
99:     full_text: str,
100:     *,
101:     contract_id: str,
102:     title: str,
103:     file_name: str,
104:     warnings: List[str],
105:     contract_type: ContractType,
106:     user_role: PartySide,
107:     jurisdiction: str,
108: ) -> AnalysisResult:
109:     logger.info("Analysing contract {} ({} chars)", contract_id, len(full_text))
110: 
111:     # 1. Clause segmentation
112:     raw_clauses = segment_clauses(full_text, contract_id=contract_id)
113:     logger.info("Segmented into {} clauses", len(raw_clauses))
114:     # P1: resolve cross-references/definitions/precedence (read-only enrichment;
115:     # no rule, severity or trigger behaviour is changed).
116:     context_bundle = resolve_context(raw_clauses)
117: 
118:     # 2. Classification + NER + obligation + risk
119:     clauses: List[Clause] = []
120:     all_obligations: List[Obligation] = []
121: 
122:     counter = 0
123:     for raw in raw_clauses:
124:         cls = classify_clause(raw.text, heading=raw.heading)
125:         extraction = extract_entities(raw.text, clause_text=raw.text)
126:         obligations = extract_obligations_from_clause(
127:             raw.clause_id,
128:             raw.text,
129:             obligation_counter=counter,
130:         )
131:         counter += len(obligations)
132:         all_obligations.extend(obligations)
133: 
134:         clause = Clause(
135:             clause_id=raw.clause_id,
136:             section_number=raw.section_number,
137:             heading=raw.heading,
138:             text=raw.text,
139:             page_hint=raw.page_hint,
140:             char_start=raw.char_start,
141:             char_end=raw.char_end,
142:             clause_types=cls.labels,
143:             entities=extraction.entities,
144:             context=context_bundle.get(raw.clause_id),
145:         )
146:         clauses.append(clause)
147: 
148:     # 3. Summary attributes
149:     summary_draft = ContractSummary(
150:         contract_id=contract_id,
151:         title=title,
152:         file_name=file_name,
153:         contract_type=contract_type,
154:         jurisdiction=jurisdiction,
155:     )
156:     summary_draft.governing_law = detect_governing_law(full_text)
157:     summary_draft.arbitration_seat = detect_arbitration_seat(full_text)
158:     summary_draft.stamp_duty_mentioned = detect_stamp_duty_mention(full_text)
159:     summary_draft.tds_mentioned = detect_tds_mention(full_text)
160:     summary_draft.gstin_mentioned = detect_gstin_mention(full_text)
161:     summary_draft.parties = _detect_parties(clauses)
162:     summary_draft.effective_date = _first_date(clauses)
163:     summary_draft.clause_count = len(clauses)
164:     summary_draft.obligation_count = len(all_obligations)
165: 
166:     # 4. Risk rules -> flags, then ML recall booster for unflagged clauses
167:     flags = apply_rules(clauses, summary_draft)
168:     flags = _augment_with_ml_risks(clauses, flags)
169: 
170:     # 5. Annotate clauses with their own risk_score
171:     for cl in clauses:
172:         cl_flags = [f for f in flags if f.clause_id == cl.clause_id]
173:         if cl_flags:
174:             top = max(cl_flags, key=lambda f: f.score)
175:             cl.risk_score = top.score
176:             cl.risk_level = top.severity
177:             cl.risk_reasons = [f.name for f in cl_flags]
178:         else:
179:             cl.risk_level = RiskSeverity.LOW
180:             cl.risk_score = 0.0
181:             cl.risk_reasons = []
182: 
183:     # 6. Aggregate contract risk
184:     from nlp.risk_scoring.scorer import score_contract
185: 
186:     overall_score, overall_level = score_contract(clauses, flags)
187:     summary_draft.overall_risk_score = overall_score
188:     summary_draft.overall_risk_level = overall_level
189:     summary_draft.high_risk_clauses = sum(
190:         1 for c in clauses if c.risk_level in (RiskSeverity.HIGH, RiskSeverity.CRITICAL)
191:     )
192:     summary_draft.missing_clauses = [
193:         f.name
194:         for f in flags
195:         if f.rule_id.startswith("MISSING_CLAUSE_") or f.rule_id == "RISK_DATA_MISSING"
196:     ]
197:     summary_draft.top_risks = sorted(
198:         flags, key=lambda f: severity_to_score(f.severity), reverse=True,
199:     )[:5]
200: 
201:     # 7. Surface runtime provenance verdicts (data-lineage only, not accuracy).
202:     analysis_warnings = list(warnings)
203:     try:
204:         from nlp import provenance as _provenance
205: 
206:         analysis_warnings.extend(_provenance.warnings())
207:     except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - provenance must never break analysis
208:         pass
209: 
210:     return AnalysisResult(
211:         contract=summary_draft,
212:         clauses=clauses,
213:         obligations=all_obligations,
214:         risks=flags,
215:         warnings=analysis_warnings,
216:     )
217:

220: # Helpers
221: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
222: 
223: 
224: _ML_FALLBACK_SCORE = {"medium": 45.0, "high": 60.0, "critical": 75.0}
225: 
226: 
227: def _augment_with_ml_risks(clauses: List[Clause], flags: List[RiskFlag]) -> List[RiskFlag]:
228:     """Add model-predicted findings for clauses the rules did not flag.
229: 
230:     The ML risk classifier is a *recall booster*: it never overrides a rule, it
231:     only surfaces additional candidates for human review. A no-op when no
232:     trained model artefact is present, so the rule-only pipeline is unaffected.
233:     """
234:     from app.models.schemas import EvidenceSpan
235:     from nlp.risk_scoring.risk_model import load_cached, predict_clause_risk
236: 
237:     if load_cached() is None:
238:         return flags
239: 
240:     flagged = {f.clause_id for f in flags if f.clause_id}
241:     extra: List[RiskFlag] = []
242:     for clause in clauses:
243:         if clause.clause_id in flagged:
244:             continue
245:         prediction = predict_clause_risk(clause.text)
246:         if prediction is None:
247:             continue
248:         extra.append(
249:             RiskFlag(
250:                 risk_id=f"{clause.clause_id}_ML_RISK_001",
251:                 clause_id=clause.clause_id,
252:                 rule_id="ML_RISK_001",
253:                 name=f"Model-detected {prediction.severity.value} risk",
254:                 severity=prediction.severity,
255:                 explanation=(
256:                     f"The ML risk classifier predicts {prediction.severity.value} severity "
257:                     f"(confidence {prediction.confidence:.0%}) from the clause wording, although "
258:                     "no explicit rule matched. Treat as a review prompt, not a definitive finding."
259:                 ),
260:                 recommendation="Manually review this clause against the standard playbook.",
261:                 score=_ML_FALLBACK_SCORE.get(prediction.severity.value, 45.0),
262:                 # P2: model-only suggestion - distinguishable and NOT evidence-backed.
263:                 source="model",
264:                 evidence_status="unverified",
265:                 evidence_spans=[
266:                     EvidenceSpan(
267:                         text=clause.text,
268:                         char_start=0,
269:                         char_end=len(clause.text),
270:                         clause_id=clause.clause_id,
271:                         role="contextual",
272:                         locator="clause_text",
273:                     )
274:                 ],
275:             )
276:         )
277:     if extra:
278:         logger.info("ML risk classifier added {} extra finding(s)", len(extra))
279:     return flags + extra

282: def _detect_parties(clauses: List[Clause]) -> List[str]:
283:     """Detect party names using NER entities + preamble + pattern-3 fallbacks."""
284:     parties: List[str] = []
285:     section_starts = re.compile(r"^\s*\d+(\.\d+)*\s*\.?\s*[A-Z]")
286:     blacklist = {
287:         "agreement", "indemnification", "confidentiality", "between",
288:         "stamp duty", "force majeure", "term and renewal", "data protection",
289:         "intellectual property", "limitation of liability", "definitions",
290:         "governing law", "dispute resolution", "termination", "miscellaneous",
291:         "notice", "payment terms", "warranty", "service levels",
292:         "change control", "acceptance", "compliance", "insurance",
293:         "audit rights", "assignment", "non-compete", "non-solicit",
294:     }
295: 
296:     def _scan(text: str) -> List[str]:
297:         """Extract party candidates from a chunk of text."""
298:         found: List[str] = []
299:         if not text:
300:             return found
301:         # 1. Suffix-based extraction (most reliable for Indian companies).
302:         pvt_suffix = re.compile(
303:             r"\b((?:[A-Z][\w'.-]+\s+){0,5}(?:Pvt\.?\s*Ltd\.?|Limited|LLP|Inc\.?|Corporation|Corp\.?|LLC|PLC))\b"
304:         )
305:         noise_words = {
306:             "having", "with", "between", "of", "the", "and", "from", "pan",
307:             "cin", "gstin", "represented", "incorporated", "registered", "its",
308:             "their", "whose", "whereas", "recital", "by", "as", "for",
309:             "annexure", "annexed", "schedule", "section", "clause",
310:             "services", "company", "agent", "customer", "resident", "client",
311:             "party", "parties", "provider", "recipient",
312:             "january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july",
313:             "august", "september", "october", "november", "december",
314:         }
315:         pan_noise = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z],?\s*(?:and\s+)?", re.IGNORECASE)
316:         # Also catch "DTwelve Accommodations Private Limited" style names
317:         # where "Private Limited" or "Pte Ltd" appears.
318:         generic_corp = re.compile(
319:             r"\b((?:[A-Z][\w'.-]+\s+){0,5}(?:Private\s+Limited|Pte\.?\s+Ltd\.?|Private\s+Ltd\.?|Ltd\.?))\b"
320:         )
321:         for pat in (pvt_suffix, generic_corp):
322:             for match in pat.finditer(text):
323:                 end = match.end()
324:                 start = match.start()
325:                 prefix = text[:start]
326:                 cut = max(prefix.rfind("\n"), prefix.rfind(". "), prefix.rfind(" ("), -1)
327:                 # Walk back through tokens but stop at noise words.
328:                 tokens_back = re.findall(r"[A-Z][\w'.-]+", text[max(0, cut + 1) : end])
329:                 kept: List[str] = []
330:                 for tok in reversed(tokens_back):
331:                     if tok.lower() in noise_words or tok.lower() in blacklist:
332:                         break
333:                     kept.append(tok)
334:                     if len(kept) >= 7:
335:                         break
336:                 if not kept:
337:                     continue
338:                 kept.reverse()
339:                 name = " ".join(kept)
340:                 name = pan_noise.sub("", name).strip().strip(",.;:")
341:                 # Strip leading noise tokens like "Private Limited" that
342:                 # bleed in from a previous match.
343:                 while name:
344:                     first = name.split()[0].lower()
345:                     if first in {"private", "limited", "pvt", "llp", "inc", "corp",
346:                                   "the", "and", "of", "company", "agent", "customer"}:
347:                         name = " ".join(name.split()[1:]).strip()
348:                     else:
349:                         break
350:                 if 4 <= len(name) <= 100 and name not in parties and name not in found:
351:                     found.append(name)
352:                 if len(found) >= 6:
353:                     return found
354:         return found
355: 
356:     # 1. Scan the heading + body of the first 3 clauses (preamble often
357:     # appears as the heading of clause 0).
358:     for c in clauses[:3]:
359:         for chunk in ((c.heading or ""), (c.text or "")[:2000]):
360:             for name in _scan(chunk):
361:                 if name not in parties:
362:                     parties.append(name)
363:             if len(parties) >= 4:
364:                 break
365: 
366:     # 2. NER entities (PARTY/ORG) from the first 6 clauses.
367:     if len(parties) < 2:
368:         for c in clauses[:6]:
369:             for ent in c.entities:
370:                 if ent.label not in {"PARTY", "ORG"}:
371:                     continue
372:                 t = (ent.text or "").strip().strip(",.;:")
373:                 if not t or len(t) > 80 or section_starts.match(t):
374:                     continue
375:                 if t.lower() in blacklist:
376:                     continue
377:                 if re.search(r"\b[A-Z][A-Za-z]+\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z]+\b", t) and t not in parties:
378:                     parties.append(t)
379:             if len(parties) >= 4:
380:                 break
381: 
382:     # 3. Preamble "between X and Y" pattern (last-ditch).
383:     if len(parties) < 2:
384:         preamble_patterns = [
385:             re.compile(
386:                 r"(?im)^\s*this\s+\w+\s+agreement\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*is\s+(?:made|entered\s+into)?\s*"
387:                 r"(?:on|as\s+of)?\s*[^\n]{0,40}?\n+\s*between\s+"
388:                 r"([^\n,;]+?)\s*(?:\(|,|having)\s*"
389:                 r".*?\s*(?:and|&)\s+"
390:                 r"([^\n,;]+?)(?:\s*\(|\s*,|\s*having|\.|\n|$)",
391:                 re.DOTALL,
392:             ),
393:             re.compile(
394:                 r"(?im)between\s+([A-Z][^\n,;(]{2,80}?)\s+(?:and|&)\s+([A-Z][^\n,;(]{2,80}?)\s*(?:\(|,|\.|having|$)",
395:             ),
396:         ]
397:         search_text = "\n".join(
398:             (c.heading or "") + "\n" + (c.text or "")[:1500] for c in clauses[:2]
399:         )
400:         for pat in preamble_patterns:
401:             m = pat.search(search_text)
402:             if not m:
403:                 continue
404:             for grp in (m.group(1), m.group(2)):
405:                 name = grp.strip().strip(",.;:")
406:                 if not name:
407:                     continue
408:                 name = re.sub(r"^\s*the\s+", "", name, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
409:                 drop = {"having", "with", "between", "and", "of", "the"}
410:                 while name and name.split()[0].lower() in drop:
411:                     name = " ".join(name.split()[1:])
412:                 while name and name.split()[-1].lower() in drop:
413:                     name = " ".join(name.split()[:-1])
414:                 if 3 <= len(name) <= 80 and name not in parties:
415:                     parties.append(name)
416:             break
417: 
418:     # Dedupe case-insensitively, prefer the most-complete spelling.
419:     deduped: List[str] = []
420:     seen_lower: set[str] = set()
421:     for name in parties:
422:         key = name.lower().strip()
423:         if key in seen_lower:
424:             continue
425:         seen_lower.add(key)
426:         deduped.append(name)
427:     return deduped[:4]
428:

430: def _first_date(clauses: List[Clause]) -> Optional[str]:
431:     """Prefer entities, then generic date search."""
432:     for c in clauses:
433:         for ent in c.entities:
434:             if ent.label == "DATE":
435:                 value = ent.text.strip()
436:                 if value and len(value) > 4:
437:                     return value
438:     generic_date_re = re.compile(
439:         r"\b(\d{1,2}\s+(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December|Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)\s+\d{2,4})\b",
440:         re.IGNORECASE,
441:     )
442:     for c in clauses[:10]:
443:         text = c.text or ""
444:         m = generic_date_re.search(text)
445:         if m:
446:             return m.group(1).strip()
447:     return None

+    # P4: enrich each clause's context bundle with the text of its related
+    # clauses so risk rules can perform whole-contract (cross-reference) checks
+    # without treating a resolved reference as proof of override.
+    clause_by_id = {c.clause_id: c for c in clauses}
+    for cl in clauses:
+        ctx = cl.context
+        if not isinstance(ctx, dict):
+            continue
+        related_ids = ctx.get("related_clause_ids") or []
+        related_texts = [
+            clause_by_id[rid].text
+            for rid in related_ids
+            if rid in clause_by_id and rid != cl.clause_id
+        ]
+        ctx = dict(ctx)
+        ctx["related_clause_texts"] = related_texts
+        cl.context = ctx
+
     flags = apply_rules(clauses, summary_draft)
